plants.name: Chrysanthemum × morifolium
plants.description: A classic autumn perennial with dense, layered blooms in many forms, including pompon, spider, and decorative types. It thrives as days shorten and is a staple of fall gardens and floral displays across the Northern Hemisphere.
plants.location: Cultivated worldwide; native to East Asia (China and Japan); widely grown in temperate gardens of North America, Europe, and Asia
plants.funFact: Chrysanthemums are short-day plants, so they set buds only when nights lengthen. In Japan, the flower is the emblem of the Imperial family and honored at the Festival of Happiness each autumn.

plants.name: Symphyotrichum novae-angliae
plants.description: A tall, bushy North American wildflower topped with clusters of daisy-like flowers with golden-yellow centers. It brightens meadows, roadsides, and prairies in late season and is an important nectar source for migrating monarch butterflies.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late summer to mid-autumn (August to October)
plants.location: Eastern and central North America, from Quebec to Alabama and west to the Rocky Mountains
plants.funFact: New England Asters close their flowers at night and on cloudy days. Their late blooms provide critical fuel for monarch butterflies on their migration to Mexico.

plants.name: Jacaranda mimosifolia
plants.description: A spectacular subtropical tree that becomes covered with clouds of trumpet-shaped lavender-blue flowers before its fernlike leaves fully emerge. Mid-October is the peak of bloom in the Southern Hemisphere spring, carpeting streets with fallen petals.
plants.bloomingSeason: Spring in the Southern Hemisphere (October to November)
plants.location: Native to South America; famously planted in Pretoria (South Africa), Sydney and Brisbane (Australia), and Buenos Aires (Argentina)
plants.funFact: Pretoria is nicknamed the 'Jacaranda City' because of its roughly 70,000 trees, and a local superstition says a jacaranda blossom falling on your head brings good luck.

plants.name: Cosmos bipinnatus
plants.description: A airy, feathery-leaved annual with saucer-shaped daisy-like flowers on tall slender stems. It blooms prolifically through summer and into autumn in mild regions, and in subtropical climates it flowers vigorously in the cooler months.
plants.bloomingSeason: Summer to first frost; autumn in warm regions
plants.location: Native to Mexico; naturalized and cultivated in North America, Europe, Asia, and Australia
plants.funFact: The name 'cosmos' comes from the Greek word for 'order' or 'harmony,' referring to the symmetrical arrangement of the petals. Spanish priests in Mexico reportedly grew them in mission gardens.
